module purpose: neorv32_wdt is a bus-programmed watchdog: a write to the control word (addr(2) = '0') sets enable, lock, strict mode and a 24-bit timeout unless the lock is set, and a write to the second word restarts the count when its data equals the constant password. Once enabled, a 24-bit counter advances on a prescaler tick taken from clkgen_i; when it equals the timeout, or when an illegal access occurs in strict mode, the module asserts the active-low reset output rstn_o and records the reset cause. Configuration and cause are readable over the bus, and clkgen_en_o exports the enable.

use-case flows.value: enable, strict-mode bit and timeout threshold written from bus data into ctrl while the lock is clear
configuration lock bit, settable only while enabled; once set it blocks configuration writes and turns each one into an illegal-access flag
counter run state: cnt_started set once the watchdog is enabled and a prescaler tick arrives
elapsed-time count advanced on each registered tick while started and compared with the timeout threshold
watchdog count cleared by a password-matched restart write or by disabling
hardware reset request on rstn_o from a timeout or from an illegal access in strict mode
reset cause recorded from the debug reset input, the timeout reset or the access reset
enable, lock, reset cause, strict bit and timeout returned on a bus read
rstn_sys_i clears configuration, counter state and reset decisions; rstn_ext_i clears the reset cause

conceptual assets.concept: Watchdog enable -- whether the watchdog counts and may issue reset requests
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow writes `ctrl.enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_enable_c);` (line 94) only when stb, rw, addr(2) = '0' and ctrl.lock = '0' hold (lines 90-93). The module's behavior depends on it: a cleared enable clears the counter (lines 131-132) and it gates cnt_started (line 130), the timeout reset (line 155), the access reset (line 156) and lock setting (line 95). It is also exported by `clkgen_en_o <= ctrl.enable;` (line 140). Integrity is Established: a corrupted enable stops or starts counting and reset generation against the written value. Availability is also Established: the value is held between writes and cleared only by rstn_sys_i (line 75). ctrl.enable stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, line 94; its GATES records target hw_rst_timeout, hw_rst_access, cnt and cnt_started). clkgen_en_o is an exit port (COPIES ctrl.enable at occurrence 2, line 140); an output that exports an enable is not excluded. bus_req_i and bus_rsp_o carry complete transactions (addr, data, ben, stb, rw; ack, err, data), so they are transport: bus_req_i.data is not a setting point, and the readback at line 109 is not an exit.

conceptual assets.concept: Configuration lock -- freezes the watchdog configuration until system reset
conceptual assets.reasoning: In the lock flow, `if (ctrl.lock = '0') then` (line 93) allows configuration writes (lines 94-97); otherwise the write sets `reset_force <= '1';` (line 99). The lock is set by `ctrl.lock <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_lock_c) and ctrl.enable;` (line 95), so only while the watchdog is enabled. That assignment sits inside the lock = '0' branch, so once set the lock is cleared only by rstn_sys_i (line 76). Integrity is Established: a cleared lock would allow the reconfiguration (disable, new timeout, strict off) that the lock forbids, and a spurious lock blocks configuration. ctrl.lock stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4, line 95; GATES ctrl.enable, ctrl.strict and ctrl.timeout at occurrence 3, line 93). Map note: the map writes the operands of line 95 as GATES (single-bit operands of a top-level and), so the flow graph lists ctrl.lock as a constant-valued source. The RTL shows that it takes the written data bit.

conceptual assets.concept: Strict-mode setting -- whether an illegal access raises a hardware reset
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow writes `ctrl.strict <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_strict_c);` (line 96) under the same conditions as the other fields (lines 90-93). It decides `hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force;` (line 156). Integrity is Established: a corrupted bit wrongly decides whether illegal accesses reset the system. ctrl.strict stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, line 96; GATES hw_rst_access at occurrence 5, line 156). The readback at line 112 goes through the transport record bus_rsp_o and is not listed.

conceptual assets.concept: Timeout threshold -- the count at which the watchdog expires
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow writes `ctrl.timeout <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_timeout_msb_c downto ctrl_timeout_lsb_c);` (line 97) while the lock is clear (line 93). The expiry compares against it: `cnt_timeout <= '1' when (cnt_started = '1') and (cnt = ctrl.timeout) else '0';` (line 144). Integrity is Established: a corrupted threshold moves the expiry and the resulting reset. Availability is Established because the value is held between writes and cleared only by rstn_sys_i (line 78). ctrl.timeout stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, line 97; CONSTRAINS cnt_timeout at occurrence 5, line 144).

conceptual assets.concept: Watchdog elapsed-time count and its running state
conceptual assets.reasoning: In the operate flow, `cnt_started <= ctrl.enable and (cnt_started or prsc_tick);` (line 130) and `cnt_inc <= prsc_tick and cnt_started;` (line 129) run the counter. It is cleared when disabled or restarted (lines 131-132) and incremented by `cnt <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(cnt) + 1);` (line 134) when cnt_inc is set. Expiry compares cnt with ctrl.timeout only while cnt_started is set (line 144). Integrity is Established: a corrupted count or started flag brings the expiry forward, delays it or suppresses it. Availability is Established under the implemented conditions: while enabled and started, the count advances once per registered tick. cnt stores the count (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4, line 134; CONSTRAINS cnt_timeout at occurrence 6) and updates itself. cnt_started stores the running state (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4, line 130; GATES cnt_timeout at occurrence 6) and also updates itself. Not listed: cnt_inc only holds the previous edge's prsc_tick and cnt_started to gate the increment (GATES cnt at occurrence 4, line 133). prsc_tick is a bit of clkgen_i (line 141). clkgen_i is the prescaler clock-enable input that times counting and expiry, so the clock-enable rule excludes it.

conceptual assets.concept: Timeout expiry decision and the timeout reset request
conceptual assets.reasoning: cnt_timeout computes the expiry comparison at line 144 (CONSTRAINED_BY cnt and ctrl.timeout, GATED_BY cnt_started, occurrence 2). `hw_rst_timeout <= ctrl.enable and cnt_timeout and prsc_tick;` (line 155) registers the reset decision. `rstn_o <= not (hw_rst_timeout or hw_rst_access);` (line 161) drives it out, and hw_rst_timeout also sets reset_cause to 10 (lines 173-174). Integrity is Established: the reset must be asserted exactly when the enabled, started counter reaches the threshold. Availability is Established under the implemented conditions: when enable is set, cnt_started is set, cnt equals ctrl.timeout and a tick occurs, hw_rst_timeout rises on the next edge and rstn_o goes low (lines 144, 155, 161). hw_rst_timeout stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3; SOURCES rstn_o at occurrence 4, an output port). rstn_o is an exit port (DERIVES_FROM hw_rst_timeout at occurrence 2). Map note: line 155 has only single-bit and operands, so the map gives hw_rst_timeout only GATED_BY records and the flow graph lists it as constant-valued. The RTL shows that it is computed from the expiry.

conceptual assets.concept: Illegal-access decision and the access-violation reset request
conceptual assets.reasoning: reset_force is set to '1' by a configuration write while locked (lines 93, 98-99) or by a restart write whose data differs from reset_pwd_c (lines 101-102, 104-105), and is cleared on every other cycle (line 88). Then `hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force;` (line 156), rstn_o is driven from it (line 161) and reset_cause is set to 11 (lines 175-176). Integrity is Established: the illegal-access flag and its reset must follow these predicates; a suppressed flag lets a locked-configuration write or a wrong password pass without the reset that strict mode requires. Availability is Established under the implemented conditions: with enable and strict set, a flagged access raises hw_rst_access on the next edge (line 156). reset_force stores the decision (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4, line 99; GATES hw_rst_access at occurrence 6). hw_rst_access stores the registered reset decision (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3; SOURCES rstn_o at occurrence 4). rstn_o is the exit port (DERIVES_FROM hw_rst_access at occurrence 2). Map note: as for line 155, line 156 appears only as GATED_BY records, so the flow graph lists hw_rst_access as constant-valued.

conceptual assets.concept: Counter restart authorization -- the password-checked restart of the watchdog count
conceptual assets.reasoning: A write with addr(2) = '1' (lines 92, 101) sets `reset_wdt <= '1';` only when `bus_req_i.data(31 downto 0) = reset_pwd_c` (lines 102-103). reset_wdt is cleared on every other cycle (line 87), and it clears the counter (lines 131-132). No line in 101-106 tests ctrl.lock, so this restart is accepted whatever the lock state. Integrity is Established: only a write equal to the constant may restart the count. A corrupted reset_wdt restarts the count without the password, which postpones expiry, or drops a valid restart. reset_wdt stores the decision (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4, line 103; GATES cnt at occurrence 5, line 131). reset_pwd_c is a constant, not a candidate.

conceptual assets.concept: Reset cause record -- which reset source last acted
conceptual assets.reasoning: In priority order, reset_cause takes 01 when rstn_dbg_i = '0' (lines 171-172), 10 on hw_rst_timeout (lines 173-174) and 11 on hw_rst_access (lines 175-176). Only rstn_ext_i clears it, to 00 (lines 168-169), and it is returned on a bus read (line 111). Integrity is Established: the reported cause must match the event that occurred, under this priority. reset_cause stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4, line 172; CARRIES bus_rsp_o.data, an output field, at occurrence 2, line 111). rstn_dbg_i sets it: it drives no SEQUENCES or RESETS record and is not wired to a sub-unit's reset, so the reset-input exclusion does not apply, and this entity reads it to decide the cause (GATES reset_cause at occurrence 2, line 171). rstn_ext_i drives RESETS reset_cause (line 168), so it is a reset input and is excluded. The readback goes through the transport record bus_rsp_o and is not listed.
